title: Ravi Karan Singh Patel v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
disposition: Writ disposed; apply and process connection claim as per law
headnote: A tenant's writ for a shop connection was disposed without any opinion on merits. If he applies and completes the formalities within ten days, the authority must process and finalise the claim as per law within one further week. The licensee had pointed to clause 4.4(a)(i) and Annexure 4.2 as that route.
facts: The petitioner, a tenant of a shop on Maheshwari Devi Road, Banda, sought an electricity connection and a decision on his representation of 6 December 2022. He said the landlord had disconnected the shop and that his business was suffering. Relying on Narayan Prasad, he contended that an occupier-tenant cannot be refused supply merely for want of the landlord's consent. The licensee answered that the Electricity Act, 2003 and the Supply Code, 2005, including Annexure 4.2 and clause 4.4(a)(i), already provide that route.

holding_units.holding: Where a tenant seeks a writ for a new shop connection and the licensee points to the application mechanism in clause 4.4(a)(i) and Annexure 4.2, the Court, without expressing any opinion on the merits, disposes the petition by consent: if the occupier applies and completes the prescribed formalities within ten days, the authority shall process and finalise the claim in accordance with law within one further week.

principle_tags.application: The Bench did not direct that the connection be granted. It left the tenant to move an application and complete the formalities the licensee had identified under clause 4.4(a)(i) and Annexure 4.2, and directed the authority to process and finalise that claim as per law within the stated time.

not_decided.point: Whether a tenant-occupier is entitled to a new connection that cannot be refused solely for want of the landlord's consent
not_decided.note: The Court declined to express any opinion on the merits and left the claim to be processed under the Code.

authorities.name: Narayan Prasad v. State of U.P. & Ors.
